fact: OK originated as a humorous abbreviation of 'oll korrect' — a playful misspelling of 'all correct' — in 1830s Boston newspapers.
example: It spread through telegraph operators who loved its brevity and is now understood in virtually every language on Earth.
source: Boston Morning Post 1839; Allen Walker Read research

fact: Emoji were created in 1999 by Japanese artist Shigetaka Kurita for a mobile carrier. The word means 'picture character' in Japanese — it has nothing to do with 'emotion.'
example: Today there are over 3600 emoji in the Unicode Standard and they're used by 92% of the online population.

fact: English spelling is chaotic because it preserved spellings from five different language invasions while pronunciation kept evolving.
example: The letters GH alone can be pronounced at least 8 different ways: ghost tough through thought cough plough hiccough.
source: History of English spelling; David Crystal

fact: The alphabet order has barely changed in 3000 years. The Phoenicians set the sequence around 1050 BCE and it passed through Greek and Latin to English almost intact.
example: Aleph Beth Gimel became Alpha Beta Gamma became A B C. The names changed but the order stuck.
source: Phoenician script research; History of writing

fact: About 80% of English vocabulary is borrowed from other languages. English is essentially a linguistic thief.
example: 'Ketchup' comes from Hokkien Chinese. 'Shampoo' is Hindi. 'Robot' is Czech. 'Safari' is Swahili. Words you use daily are secretly foreign.
